sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F5][D161][F6][D200][F7][D238].
The FY2022 increase came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion on lower realized commodity prices, partly offset by higher sales volumes [F8][D274][P47].
Crude oil was 66.3% of FY2025 revenue and contributed just 0.1pp of the 4.9% revenue growth [D551][D553][D342].
The U.S. was 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and contributed 5.7pp of growth, while non-U.S. added 2.0pp [D382][D384][D400].
Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in FY2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% in FY2025 while basic EPS fell 18.7%, as the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D343][D344][D356].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6% in FY2025 against revenue growth of 4.9% [D352][D342].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
D&A rose $1.9 billion in FY2025 on the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes, lifting D&A to 19.5% of revenue from 17.5% [P22][D330][D296].
SG&A fell $265 million in FY2025 on the absence of $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses, partly offset by restructuring severance [P23].
The FY2025 effective tax rate of 36.9% exceeded the 32.4% of FY2024, and net margin of 15.4% sat below the 18.7% of FY2024 [D332][D298][F30][F29].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.07x window median [F59][F20][D333][D855].
The FY2025 decrease in operating cash flow from $20.1 billion in FY2024 came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by Marathon Oil operations [P6][F58].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 against a 12.2% window median, and capex was 1.35x D&A in FY2022 [D833][D834][D228].
Stock-based compensation was 1.7% of operating cash flow in FY2025, so it does not distort conversion [D334].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion at FY2025, up 13.4%, with a current ratio of 1.30x against a 1.45x window median [D335][D357][F153][D843].
Net cash is not reported after FY2020 because long-term debt is missing from the pack, so no leverage rank against peers is available [F157].
FY2025 uses of cash were $12.6 billion of capital spending, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sales [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, above the 30% framework floor [D339][F59][P31].
Revenue in the table is a later recast in every year: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion against $58.9 billion as first reported [F10][X10].
Growth and margin comparisons that mix recast and first-reported years are not like-for-like, so the revenue trend above should be read with that caveat.
Long-term debt is absent before FY2017 and after FY2020, and short-term investments are missing in FY2021 [X204][F157][X183][X184].
Net cash and debt growth cannot be tracked across the full window, which limits any leverage conclusion.
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion [F8][D274].
The decline was price-led rather than volume-led, so it reflects the commodity cycle more than a loss of franchise [P47].
Whether FY2026 revenue exceeds the FY2025 recast level of $51.8 billion, reported in the FY2026 10-K, would confirm the resumed growth [F10].
Whether net margin holds above the 17.9% window median or slips toward the 15.4% FY2025 level, shown in the FY2026 10-K, marks the margin trend [D831][F30].
Whether operating cash flow stays above the $19.8 billion FY2025 level, disclosed in the FY2026 10-K, tests the cash trend against lower prices [F59].
